crime.value: Murder by poisoning (grapejuice) and hair harvesting; central question: how did Aunt Abbie obtain the victim's hair if she fell into the gorge?
crime.quote: She placed the half-full cup on the marble-topped table at her side... the copper-red strand glinting against the half-finished rose.

victim.value: Marty's daughter, a young red-haired woman visiting from the city; killable because she is an orphan ('You're all alone?'), has no local ties, and her distinctive red hair is needed for Aunt Abbie's hair wreath.
victim.quote: You're all alone?... Except for us... Such pretty red hair... I just got the rose left.

closed_world.value: Aunt Abbie's isolated cabin in the hills, reached only by a rough walk through boulder-strewn terrain; the girl is physically isolated and dependent on Melinda and Aunt Abbie.
closed_world.quote: The cabin squatted beneath bowed trees... goin' on fifty year... quite a piece. Rough ground.

culprit_and_motive.value: Aunt Abbie, the elderly record keeper with 'second sight'; motive is to complete her hair wreath memorial—the victim's red hair is the final 'rose' needed to finish the family death record.
culprit_and_motive.quote: I just got the rose left... Such pretty, pretty red hair... Aunt Abbie never snipped a live lock. Never.

resolution.value: Melinda gradually realizes the logical impossibility of Aunt Abbie's account: the girl could not have fallen into the gorge AND provided her hair through Aunt Abbie's ritual. Melinda accepts the truth through deduction and her knowledge of Aunt Abbie's methods.
resolution.quote: How had Aunt Abbie gone through the rites... how had Aunt Abbie gone through the rites... spry enough to spring up the sheer face of the gorge—with scissors, hair and a mirror in her hand.

investigator.value: Melinda, the victim's cousin and accomplice/witness; through her perspective we see the gradual realization of Aunt Abbie's crime, though she ultimately accepts it with 'pride-filled mind.'
investigator.quote: Melinda's sorrowful, pride-filled mind knew perplexity... Melinda heaved a final sigh of acceptance.
